requirement_summary: 02_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS_AND_PROGRAMS.md FR-META-009 Decision Propagation: '의존 하위 결과의 FAIL/HOLD/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN/INCONCLUSIVE/UNKNOWN은 상위 Claim에 전파한다. Critical dependency가 미검증이면 전체 PASS로 평균화하지 않는다.'
subject: SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.decisionPropagationCheck via assurance.decision.propagation-check; contracts/decision-propagation-check.v1.schema.json (NEW)
coverage_notes: decisionPropagationCheckNeverAveragesAnUnresolvedCriticalDependencyIntoPass is the direct test of the requirement's named negative case: a NOT_RUN critical dependency alongside an otherwise-PASS dependency set forces HOLD, not PASS -- the critical-unresolved branch is checked before the all-PASS branch in the fixed precedence, so there is no code path by which a critical-but-unverified dependency could be silently averaged away. decisionPropagationCheckLetsANonCriticalUnresolvedDependencyReachOnlyInconclusive proves the distinction the requirement draws is real: the identical UNKNOWN status on a non-critical dependency reaches the weaker INCONCLUSIVE rather than HOLD, so criticality genuinely changes the computed outcome rather than being an unused input field. decisionPropagationCheckForcesBlockedAsTheMostSevereEvenWithOtherStatusesPresent proves the precedence ordering itself is real and fixed (BLOCKED outranks FAIL outranks HOLD outranks INCONCLUSIVE), not first-match-in-array-order or caller-selectable.
open_gap: Operates on a caller-supplied dependency list (dependency_id/status/critical); there is no live claim-dependency graph runtime in this codebase that actually produces this list from real sub-claim execution results (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system integration' pattern as every other real-computation closure this session). The requirement's broader context (this being about hierarchical Claim/sub-Claim structures within ONSure's own Final/Certificate assembly) is not modeled beyond the single-level dependency-list aggregation this operation performs -- multi-level propagation (a HOLD produced by this operation itself becoming one dependency of a higher-level claim) is not tested, though the schema's own output shape (propagated_status drawn from the same enum family as input dependency status) is designed to compose that way if a caller chose to chain calls.
